title: NVR: Vector Runahead on NPUs for Sparse Memory Access
problem: Sparse DNNs suffer from irregular memory access patterns causing high cache miss rates and stalls, negating computational benefits of sparsity when dealing with reduced wall-clock execution time.
motivation: Model pruning and sparsity are increasingly used to reduce parameter count, but irregular memory access patterns from sparsity create cache-miss bottlenecks that offset gains.
method: NVR adapts runahead execution to NPU architecture as a decoupled, speculative, lightweight hardware sub-thread that runs ahead to prefetch data, reducing cache misses without requiring compiler support or algorithmic changes; operates with <5% hardware overhead.
key_novelty: Runahead prefetching mechanism specialized for NPU architecture, providing general micro-architectural solution for sparse DNN cache misses without compiler/algorithmic modification.
contributions: Runahead prefetching adaptation to NPU-specific architecture
Lightweight decoupled sub-thread design with <5% hardware overhead
General solution requiring no compiler or algorithmic support
90% cache miss reduction vs SOTA prefetching; 4x average speedup on sparse workloads; 5x benefit from 16KB cache vs 2x from enlarged L2
limitations: Not discussed; focus is on prefetching design.
primary_theme: Runahead prefetching for sparse DNN cache-miss mitigation on NPUs
